 Older adults urged to seek help with their Medicare plan during the open enrollment period. (Spectrum News 1) 
 Federal healthcare programs' open enrollment kicks off
 BY 
 Reena Diamante 
 Washington, D.C. 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 PM ET Oct. 30, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 5:00 PM EDT Oct. 30, 2026 
 SHARE 
 Open enrollment for Medicare is underway and the Affordable Care Marketplace opens on Nov. 1.
 If you're in the market for health insurance for next year, there are some changes you should know about before signing up. For Medicare, there are two big differences coming in 2027: work requirements and restrictions on what non-citizens are eligible.
 "These changes will only apply to people ages 19 to 64. So, children should not be affected by these new work requirements, even if their parents are. Also important to keep in mind that many adults will be exempt from some of these new requirements. So, according to these new work requirements, in order to get or keep Medicaid, people will need to show one of four things. They either have to have monthly income above $580, they have to work, volunteer, be in school, or participate in a job program for at least 80 hours a month. They have to be in school at least half time, or they have to qualify for an exemption. And there are several categories of exemption," said Claire Heyison, a senior policy analyst for the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities.
 Some of those exemptions include pregnant people, caregivers for children under the age of 14 or the disabled, and people with serious or complex health issues that make it difficult to work.
 The other big change to Medicaid will be for who is eligible for people who are not citizens of the United States. In 2027, only lawfully permanent residents, Cuban and Haitian entrants, and individuals lawfully residing under a Compact of Free Association will be able to be covered.
 "With these changes, we expect to see again more people uninsured, more people using these safety net resources, and you know, delaying care, and creating more strain on these safety net clinics," Heyison said.
 There are also changes coming to the Affordable Care Act Marketplace, which saw a 13% drop year over year from February 2025 to February 2026 in enrollment. Premiums are set to go up for everyone after the expiration of tax credits.
 "That greatly increased the share of the total premium that people are responsible for paying. That law will take financial help away from hundreds of thousands of people with lawful immigration statuses including people granted asylum, refugees, and people granted humanitarian parole," said Heyison.
 The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid do have some good news on the prescription drug front: they expect out of pocket drug costs to come down over $600 million next year, depending on what plan you end up on.
